Name: Department of consumer and worker protection and fire department authority to seal the premises of retailers of powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, or storage batteries.

Summary: This legislation would lower the threshold needed for the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP) or the Fire Department (FDNY) to seal the premises of retailers that violate local laws establishing safety standards for the distribution, sale, lease, and rental of powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, or storage batteries for such devices.  Sealing would be permitted after a retailer received violations on at least two occasion in a two-year period; whereas currently, premises can only be sealed after a retailer receives violations on at least three occasions during a 3-year period.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to department of consumer and worker protection and fire department authority to seal the premises of retailers of powered bicycles, powered mobility devices, or storage batteries

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Subdivision i of section 20-610 of the administrative code of the city of New York, as amended by local law number 50 for the year 2024, is amended to read as follows:
 i. The commissioner, or the fire commissioner, after providing notice and an opportunity to be heard, shall be authorized to order the sealing of any premises where any person has been found:
1. to have violated subdivisions a, b, or c of this section, or any rules promulgated pursuant thereto, on at least [three] 2 occasions within a [three-year] 2-year period; or 
2. to have violated any [rule promulgated pursuant to] provision of this section, or any rules promulgated pursuant to this section, on at least [three] 3 occasions within a [three-year] 3-year period.
§ 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
